labDescription: Manage the connected lab server. Tauri remote mode uses this server without requiring synchronization.
labIntro: Start with shared inference, invite members, then choose your model.
labGuideServerText: Run these commands at the repository root after installing Docker Compose. Make lab-data writable by the app UID/GID (default 1000:1000). The app binds to 127.0.0.1:8000; configure an HTTPS reverse proxy for remote access and keep one app worker. Sign in as the existing administrator, save and test shared inference, then enable Lab mode with your current password.
labGuideOllama: Ollama · a starting point for simple setup and small groups. After installation, run ollama serve and pull a model in another terminal.
labGuideVllm: vLLM · consider for concurrent requests on a GPU server. Prepare supported hardware and install vLLM. EasyPaper requires cache_salt support and access to the server-root /openapi.json; test the connection.
labGuideModels: Example starting points: evaluate Qwen3 4B for a smaller trial and 8B for a quality comparison. These are examples, not a claim of best or latest models. Compare translation quality, latency and long-document memory on actual papers. VRAM depends on quantization, context and concurrency.
labGuideNetwork: The URL is reached by the EasyPaper server, not your browser. For a host engine from Docker, use host.docker.internal and configure the engine to bind to an interface reachable from the container. Restrict access with a firewall. Allowed and default models must exactly match served IDs.
labGuideMembersText: Administrator: enter a username in Members and create the account. Leave the initial password blank to generate one. Share the displayed password with that member; they change it on first login. Document spaces are separated by account, with no separate space creation button. On desktop, use Data → Server connection with the same server and account.
labGuideCli: Personal CLI is optional. Operators configure deploy/lab/runner.example.json and easypaper-lab-runner.service, then build CLI images or rootfs following docs/lab-mode.md. Match the runner socket group to the app GID. With automatic provisioning enabled, the first CLI status/login/inference creates a private UID and home. Members choose and save their provider, then connect their personal CLI. Local PC credentials are not transferred. Antigravity needs operator-managed authentication integration.
labHelp_enabled: Enter the administrator password and save to apply.
labHelp_password: The password of the signed-in administrator.
labHelp_engine: Consider Ollama for simple setup or vLLM for GPU concurrency.
labHelp_models: Enter installed model IDs, one per line. Example: qwen3:4b
labHelp_default-model: Enter one ID from the allowed models list.
labHelp_total-limit: Total concurrent requests. Starting defaults are Ollama 2 / vLLM 8; tune after measuring server load.
labHelp_user-limit: Concurrent requests per person. Start with 1.
labHelp_api-key: Inference server authentication key. Blank preserves the saved key.
labHelp_username: Use letters, digits, underscore, dot or hyphen. Cannot change in Lab mode.
labHelp_member-password: 8–128 characters. Leave blank to generate a temporary password.
labHelp_personal-provider: Choose the shared engine or an operator-provisioned personal CLI.
labHelp_personal-model: For shared inference use an allowed model ID; for CLI use its provider model ID.
labSystemdHelp: Without Docker: prepare Python and backend dependencies, then adapt the service user and paths to your server. Prepare the runner service for personal CLI. Run these commands after configuring the templates.
labPreviewSpace: Document space for {{name}} → first sign-in → password change → save personal model. This preview does not create an account.
labPreviewInvalid: Enter 1–80 letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens.
labCliReady: Operator has prepared the runner and CLI runtime
labCliNext: Next: save personal provider → connect personal CLI → authenticate → check connection status
labCliWait: The operator must first prepare the runner socket and CLI runtime.
labWizardServer: Install on your server over SSH. Prepare Git, Docker Compose and Caddy first. Replace the example server IP and domain with your own.
labWizardEngine: Install Ollama on the same server, then follow the demo. Restrict port 11434 to Docker access with your firewall.
labWizardMembers: The administrator enables Lab and creates member accounts. Members sign in using the HTTPS address and temporary password they receive.
labWizardInvite: Username: alice → Create account → Temporary password
labWizardLogin: alice → Sign in → Change temporary password
labWizardSpace:
alice’s documents
Upload a paper → Start reading
labWizardDemo: Illustrative playback · No commands or settings are executed
labWizardDetails: Advanced setup · systemd, vLLM and personal CLI
labWizardHosting: Point the domain DNS A record to the server public IP. Open ports 80 and 443; forward them to the server if behind a router. For institutional servers, ask your administrator for external access.
labWizardProxy: On the server, open sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile and add this block. Caddy forwards HTTPS traffic to EasyPaper inside the server.
labWizardRemote: Open https://your-domain on your PC. localhost refers to the current computer, so it cannot address your remote Lab server.
labScenePrerequisites: Connect over SSH and check the required tools. If a command is missing, use the installation links first.
labSceneInstall: Clone the repository and start the service. The default data owner is 1000:1000. Timing and logs are illustrative.
labSceneAdmin: Open the HTTPS address on your PC, sign in as administrator, then open Settings → Lab. Change the initial default credentials on the server before public exposure.
labSceneOllama: Install Ollama on the Lab server. See its installation guide for server-specific requirements such as GPU drivers.
labSceneModel: Restart the engine and download the example model. Actual download time depends on your network and model size.
labSceneInvite: Leave the initial password blank to generate one. Privately share the displayed password and HTTPS address with the member. This password is only an example.
labSceneFirstLogin: For a new installation, change the administrator password before public exposure. Open this SSH tunnel in a terminal on your PC to access the server privately.
labSceneFirstAccount: With the tunnel running, open http://localhost:18000 on your PC, sign in with admin / admin, then change credentials in Settings → Account. Here localhost is the SSH tunnel entrance. Existing installations use their existing administrator account.
